instruction: GUI-only requirement: Complete the task entirely in the launched OpenStudio Application graphical user interface. Do not open Terminal or a shell; do not run Ruby, Python, OpenStudio CLI, EnergyPlus command-line tools, shell commands, or helper scripts; do not edit OSM/OSW files directly outside the GUI. Use only OpenStudio Application GUI tools, dialogs, and built-in save/export commands. Two-Story OpenStudio GUI Model. Work in the opened OpenStudio Application and build the model from scratch; there are no init_file inputs or local reference images for this case. Use the OpenStudio Application tabs and dialogs to create the geometry, spaces, thermal zones, simple ideal-loads HVAC metadata, thermostats, and fixed windows. Save only the completed model as /home/user/Desktop/result.osm using the OpenStudio Application save/save-as workflow; do not create workflow.osw, run/eplusout.sql, or any manually edited workflow artifact. Create 2 building stories, 6 spaces, and 6 thermal zones. Use these exact OS:Space names: Ground North, Ground South, Ground East, Upper North, Upper South, and Upper East. Every space must be assigned to a building story and a thermal zone, and each space must have more than 0.05 m2 of floor area. Model the enclosure with 38 total OS:Surface objects, split into 6 Floor surfaces, 6 RoofCeiling surfaces, and 26 Wall surfaces; the surface Outside Boundary Condition counts should be exactly 3 Ground, 17 Outdoors, and 18 Surface. Add 14 OS:SubSurface objects, all of them FixedWindow windows, with total fixed-window area 92.40 m2 within +/-0.50 m2. Include exactly 6 OS:ZoneHVAC:IdealLoadsAirSystem objects, 6 OS:ZoneHVAC:EquipmentList objects, and 6 OS:ThermostatSetpoint:DualSetpoint objects. Set the geometry so the overall surface-geometry bounding box spans 16.00 m in X, 14.00 m in Y, and 7.00 m in Z, each within +/-0.05 m. The total floor surface area must be 448.00 m2 within +/-0.50 m2, and the total exterior wall gross area must be 420.00 m2 within +/-0.50 m2. Other object handles, schedules, construction names, material details, and serializer ordering may vary as long as the saved OpenStudio model satisfies these stated GUI-created model requirements.
